newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania prime minister seeks state of emergency.
newsitem.headline: Albania prime minister seeks state of emergency.

text.p: Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi asked parliament on Monday to introduce a state of emergency in the southern town of Vlore to quell disorders in which three people have died, state television said.

In his address to the chamber, dominated by supporters of right-wing President Sali Berisha, Meksi denounced rioting in the city as "violent actions of terrorist groups". Debate was proceeding throughout the evening.

The television said Interior Minister Halit Shamata backed introduction of emergency measures. It said he told parliament that the anger of Vlore residents at losing their savings in a pyramid investment scheme that collapsed last week "has nothing to do with terrorist and anti-constitutional acts".
Two demonstrators died in Monday's incidents, one of a bullet wound, the other of a heart attack. A third man died in initial clashes on Sunday night.

Protesters blaming Berisha and his government for the loss of their savings threw stones and furniture at riot police after five days of largely peaceful marches in the town. They later were locked in a standoff outside the police station.
By Monday evening, all protesters had cleared the area around the police station and the city was quiet.
